text:
Alex: quick heads-up — we're adding corr-id/span signals into the console dashboards for the new routing/quotas rollout. need runtime + infra input on propagation semantics and sampling cost.
Priya: thanks. do you mean a per-request correlation id propagated across services, and a sampled flag exposed to metrics?
Alex: yep. goal is dashboard panels that can 1) show sampled vs total request counts, 2) rollups by route/model, and 3) ability to link a trace/span from the UI.
Ryan: :eyes: storage/ingest cost is the big one. if every request writes a trace link we'll explode metrics cardinality. need a sampling plan or tag-only path.
Jasper: agree. runtime can emit a compact tag like `rw.corr=true` + `rw.corr.id` only when sampled. non-sampled requests can set `rw.corr=0` so dashboards can still show totals without high-cardinality ids.
Priya: implementation idea: edge assigns `x-rw-corr: <uuid>` and `x-rw-sampled: 1|0`. internal services propagate both headers. sampler at ingress decides sample_rate per-customer/route.
Emma: from product/UX: important for customers to understand what "sampled" means in the UI. we want a toggle: "show traces (sampled only)" vs "show aggregated metrics (all requests)". also show sampling rate per-panel.
Ryan: technical constraints: metrics pipelines accept boolean labels and low-cardinality tag values. we can add `sampled:true/false` as a label. the full corr-id should not be a metric label. instead we create an index that maps sampled corr-ids -> trace links stored in a separate trace service. dashboards query that store on click.
Alex: sounds good. so panels should call console API: 1) metrics query for counts with `sampled=true/false`, 2) when user clicks an item, call trace svc with corr-id to open spans.
Priya: runtime change: we can add header injection and KV cache propagation for `x-rw-corr`. also add an internal sampling decision header `x-rw-sample-rate` so downstream can make consistent decisions. will add a toggle for deterministic sampling by customer id.
Jasper: for tracing we should standardize span tags: `rw.corr_id`, `rw.sampled` and attach `rw.route` so trace-search can filter. export only for sampled traces.
Ryan: ops note — need quota on trace-store writes and a throttling fallback. if trace-store is saturated, respond with `x-rw-trace-accepted: 0` and still surface aggregated metrics.
Emma: UX: include small indicator in the request timeline when trace is unavailable due to quota (tooltip: "trace not captured — sampling/quota").
telemetry-bot: new proposal created: https://go/internal/discussion/1911234000-corrid-metrics (added Priya, Ryan, Jasper)
Alex: next steps: Priya/Runtime to draft header + sampling contract (PR by Tue), Ryan/Infra to propose trace-store quotas + fallback, Jasper to list tag schema, Emma will mock the UX flows. sync Thurs 10am if needed.
Priya: I'll put a short spec in the repo: header names, deterministic sampling algorithm, and expected metric tags.
Ryan: I'll add expected metrics: `dashboard.requests.total`, `dashboard.requests.sampled`, `dashboard.trace_links.created`, and SLA alerts for trace-store lag.
Jasper: also recommend a short eval: run with 1% sample for 48h and measure additional qps on trace-store and query latency in console.
Emma: thanks all — important for the rollout. :thumbsup:
Alex: great. ping me once PRs are up and I'll update the rollout checklist (canary phases + opt-in flags).
Ryan: noted — will add a canary policy to avoid noisy dashboards during initial rollout.
Priya: filing the runtime PR now, will @mention the thread when ready.
Alex: thanks — closing this thread for now, will reopen after the specs land.
